## ArtNet

verbs Store, Delete, Copy, Cut, Paste, Move, Insert, Compact, List, Info, Assign, Unassign · default verb Info (`ArtNet <ids>` = `Info ArtNet <ids>`) · rights Guest: List, Info · Setup: Store, Delete, Copy, Cut, Paste, Move, Insert, Compact, Assign, Unassign · tree `Root.ShowData.Protocols.DMXProtocols.Lines`

```
Store ArtNet [<n>] ["name"] /Network <name> [/Mode Output|Input] [/LocalUniverse <u> /Amount <n> /PortAddress <net.sub.uni>] | Assign Universe <u> Thru <v> At ArtNet <n> [/Universe <a>] | Assign ArtNet <n> At Universe <u> | Set ArtNet <n> "PortAddress"|"Rate"|… <value>
```

An Art-Net 4 line: one DMX Protocols row on its network — Mode Output sends its run of local universes (LocalUniverse and the Amount after it) as Port-Addresses from PortAddress on (typed 5 or 0.0.5), to the nodes ArtPoll finds (or unicast to Target) at its own Rate, never above a node's refresh rate; Mode Input brings them into the local ones, at its InputPriority. List ArtNet shows each line's run and live state; Info ArtNet the protocol and the nodes heard.

Examples:

```
Store ArtNet 1 "Truss" /Network "Rig" /LocalUniverse 33 /Amount 4 /PortAddress 0.2.0
Assign Universe 33 Thru 36 At ArtNet 1 /Universe 0.2.0
Assign ArtNet 2 At Universe 50 /Universe 0.0.5
Set ArtNet 1 "Sync" On
Unassign ArtNet 1
```

Related: `network`, `assign`, `universe`

Options:

- `/Network <network>` (Store): The network it is on
- `/Mode <mode>` (Store): Output (local universes go out) or Input (the protocol's come in)
- `/LocalUniverse <universe>` (Store): The first local universe the line carries
- `/Amount <count>` (Store): How many local universes from LocalUniverse
- `/PortAddress <universe>` (Store): The Art-Net universe LocalUniverse is on the wire; the rest follow on
- `/Universe <address>` (Assign): The protocol universe the run starts at (sACN n, Art-Net Net.SubNet.Universe)

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Name" | text | Setup | show | display name |
| "Note" | text | Setup | show | operator note |
| "Locked" | On/Off | Setup | show | protect from edits |
| "Hidden" | On/Off | Setup | show | hide from operator views |
| "Paint" | #rrggbb, a palette colour, Theme "<slot>" or none | Setup | show | its colour on screen: #rrggbb, a palette colour, Theme "<slot>" (the viewer's theme), or none = its tags', then the pool's |
| "Icon" | icon name | Setup | show | a standard icon's name |
| "Network" | Network name or number | Setup | show | the network the line uses (created if the show has none by that name) |
| "Mode" | Output/Input | Setup | show | Output (its local universes go out) or Input (the protocol's universes come in); Assign's order sets it too |
| "LocalUniverse" | 1–65535 | Setup | show | the first local universe the line carries (a universe by number: moving a universe never moves the line) |
| "Amount" | 0–4096 | Setup | show | how many local universes from LocalUniverse (0 = none) |
| "Target" | text | Setup | show | Output: unicast IPv4 address, none = multicast (sACN) / ArtPoll + broadcast (Art-Net). Input: accept only this source, none = any |
| "Rate" | 1–60 | Setup | show | Output: frames per second (1–60, default 30): the line samples the engine's newest 60 Hz frame; never above what an Art-Net node reports |
| "Send" | Full/Changes | Setup | show | Output: Full (every universe every time) or Changes (a change at once and 3 repeats, then a keep-alive every second) |
| "PacketGap" | 0–2000 | Setup | show | Output: µs between universes, for old nodes that drop bursts (0–2000; never more than half of one send period in all) |
| "Sync" | On/Off | Setup | show | Output: send ArtSync / an E1.31 sync packet after the line's universes (pixel and video nodes) |
| "InputPriority" | Super/Prog/Highest/High/LTP/Low/Lowest | Setup | show | Input: the band its DMX competes at in Prio universes (Super … Lowest) |
| "Enabled" | On/Off | Setup | show | the line runs |
| "PortAddress" | text | Setup | show | the ArtNet universe LocalUniverse is on the wire; the rest follow on (0.0.0–127.15.15) |


## Asset

aliases `assets` · verbs Info, Import (reach Drive), Delete, Label, List (reach Drive) · default verb Info (`Asset <ids>` = `Info Asset <ids>`) · rights Guest: Info, List · Program: Import, Delete, Label · tree `Root.ShowData.Assets.Files`

```
Import Asset "<root>" "path" ["name"] | Delete|Label Asset <n> | List Asset [/Missing] [/Verify]
```

A large file on an asset drive (decisions §8): the show keeps its root, path, SHA-256 and size, never the file. List Asset shows whether each is on this station; a missing asset is listed, never a crash. Preloading into memory and the operator-approved media sync come later.

Examples:

```
Import Asset "Video" "clips/intro.mov"
List Asset /Missing
List Asset /Verify      -- also checks every SHA-256 (slow)
```

Related: `assetroot`, `image`

Options:

- `/Hash <sha256>` (Import): The file's SHA-256 (64 hex digits)
- `/Size <bytes>` (Import): The file's size in bytes
- `/Verify` (List): Check every file's hash
- `/Missing` (List): Only the files that are missing


## AssetRoot

aliases `assetroots` · verbs Info, Store, Delete, Label, List · default verb Info (`AssetRoot <ids>` = `Info AssetRoot <ids>`) · rights Guest: Info, List · Setup: Store, Delete, Label · tree `Root.ShowData.Assets.Roots`

```
Store AssetRoot "Video" | Set AssetRoot "Video" "Folder" <path|none> | Delete|Label AssetRoot <n> | List AssetRoot
```

A named place for large show-critical media that stays outside the .luma (decisions §8). The show names the root; each station maps it to a folder or drive of its own (station-local, like a network to a NIC).

Examples:

```
Store AssetRoot "Video"
Set AssetRoot "Video" "Folder" "/Volumes/Media/Video"
List AssetRoot
```

Related: `asset`, `image`

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Folder" | text or None | Setup | station | this station's folder or drive for the asset root (None = no files here) |


## Attribute

aliases `att`, `attributes` · verbs Select, At, Assign, Move, List, Info, Edit · default verb Select (`Attribute <ids>` = `Select Attribute <ids>`) · rights Guest: List, Info, Edit · Playback: Select, At · Setup: Assign, Move

```
Attribute <name> At <value> | Attribute <name> Fade|Delay <s>|Cue | Assign [UserProfile [<n>|"name"]] Attribute <names> At [UserProfile] FeatureGroup <g> [/WithSubs|/Only] | Set Attribute <name> "Readout" Percent|Physical | "Resolution" Coarse|Fine|Ultra | Move [UserProfile] Attribute <names> At <n> | At FeatureGroup <g> [<n>] | List [UserProfile] Attribute [/New] [/Unused] [/Hint] [FixtureType "x"] | Info [UserProfile] Attribute <names> | Default [UserProfile] Attribute /New | Edit [UserProfile] Attribute [/New|/Hint|/Unused] [/By FixtureType]
```

A fixture attribute (decisions §30 "12f-a"). Calling it sets a programmer value on the selection (Attribute "Pan" At 120). The show's definition says which feature group it is in — cue timing per feature group reads it; your profile has its own grouping (UserProfile Attribute …) for your encoder bar. A patch that brings an attribute nobody has seen places it by the resolver's rules (marked new) in the show and in every profile, and each user is asked. Names: quoted when they hold spaces, + joins, a quoted * is a pattern.

Examples:

```
Attribute "Dimmer" Fade 2   -- the selection's Dimmer values fade 2 s when stored
Attribute "Pan" At 120                              -- programmer
Assign Attribute "Zoom" At FeatureGroup "FX"              -- the show's, at the bottom
Assign UserProfile Attribute "Zoom" At UserProfile FeatureGroup "Beam" -- yours
Assign Attribute "Shutter2*" At FeatureGroup "Shutter"
Move Attribute "Zoom" At FeatureGroup "FX" 3
Info Attribute "Pan Invert"                         -- why it is where it is
List UserProfile Attribute /New
Default UserProfile Attribute /New                  -- keep where your rules put them
Edit UserProfile Attribute /New                     -- your board, the new ones
```

Related: `featuregroup`, `attributerule`, `encoderbar`, `default`, `userprofile`

Options:

- `/New`: Only the attributes a patch brought, not answered yet
- `/Unused`: Only attributes no patched fixture uses
- `/Hint`: Only placements from a hint or a guess
- `/By <key>`: What to sort, split, compact or show by (Number, Name, Family, MainFirst, Address, FixtureType)
- `/WithSubs`: Move its sub-attributes with it
- `/Only`: Move only this attribute

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Readout" | Percent/Physical | Setup | show | how its value reads: Percent or Physical |
| "Resolution" | Coarse/Fine/Ultra | Setup | show | its encoder resolution |


## AttributeRule

aliases `attributerules` · verbs Store, Move, Delete, List, Info · default verb Info (`AttributeRule <ids>` = `Info AttributeRule <ids>`) · rights Guest: List, Info · Setup: Store, Move, Delete

```
Store [UserProfile] AttributeRule "pattern" FeatureGroup <g> [Feature "f"] [/Keyword] | Move AttributeRule <n> At <m> | Delete AttributeRule <n> | List AttributeRule [/Learned] | Info AttributeRule <n> | "name"
```

The resolver's rules (decisions §30 "12f-a"): where an attribute nobody has seen goes — the show's, or a profile's own (UserProfile AttributeRule …). Tried in order, the first match wins: * = any characters, {n} = digits, case-insensitive, whole name. A stored rule is learned: it is someone's own choice and wins over the standard table. Info with a name says which rule would place it.

Examples:

```
Store AttributeRule "Pixel*" FeatureGroup "FX"
Store UserProfile AttributeRule "Gobo{n}*" FeatureGroup "Gobo"
Move AttributeRule 15 At 3
List AttributeRule /Learned
Info AttributeRule "PixelMSpeed"
```

Related: `attribute`, `featuregroup`

Options:

- `/Learned`: Only the rules learned here
- `/Keyword`: A keyword rule (the word anywhere in the name)

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Pattern" | text | Setup | show | the names it places: * = any characters, {n} = digits, case-insensitive, whole name (a change makes it learned) |
| "FeatureGroup" | text | Setup | show | the feature group it places into, by name or number (a change makes it learned) |
| "Feature" | text | Setup | show | the feature inside the group, or none |


## AttributeTemplate

aliases `attributetemplates` · verbs Call, List · default verb List (`AttributeTemplate <ids>` = `List AttributeTemplate <ids>`) · rights Guest: List · Setup: Call

```
List AttributeTemplate | Call AttributeTemplate "<name>" At ShowData | UserProfile [<n>|"name"]
```

A built-in grouping recipe (decisions §33 89): feature groups and the rules that place each attribute ("GDTF standard": GDTF's groups; "LumaCore FX": gobos, prisms and spins under FX). Call applies one once — the show's grouping (cue timing per feature group, Setup) or a profile's own (its encoder bar); learned rules stay. Asks first.

Examples:

```
List AttributeTemplate
Call AttributeTemplate "LumaCore FX" At ShowData
Call AttributeTemplate "GDTF standard" At UserProfile
```

Related: `attribute`, `featuregroup`, `attributerule`

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|


## Blind

verbs On, Off, Toggle, List, Info · default verb Toggle (`Blind` = `Toggle Blind`) · rights Guest: List, Info · Playback: On, Off, Toggle

```
Blind | On Blind | Off Blind | Toggle Blind
```

Program without changing the live output: while Blind is on, your programmer stays out of the DMX output. Per user. The output effect comes with the render engine; today Blind keeps the state, status and key LED.

Examples:

```
Blind         -- toggle
On Blind      -- switch on
Off Blind     -- switch off
```

Related: `blind`, `highlight`, `freeze`, `solo`

## Clock

aliases `timing` · verbs Info · default verb Info (`Clock` = `Info Clock`) · rights Guest: Info

```
Clock [/watch[=<ms>]]
```

Display the current wall-clock time (HH:MM:SS.mmm). Add `/watch` to live-refresh. Use `Info Clock` for the session clock: its offset to the LumaSession master, round trip, jitter, drift and PTP.

Examples:

```
clock           -- show current time
clock /watch    -- live clock (200ms)
```

Related: `watch`


## Cue

aliases `cues` · verbs Store, List, Info · default verb Goto (`Cue <ids>` = `Goto Cue <ids>`) · ids decimal (1.10 = 1.1) · **planned — not built yet:** Delete, Move · rights Guest: List, Info · Program: Store, Delete, Move

```
Cue <n> [Sequence <m>] | Store Cue <n> [Sequence <m>] | List Cue [Sequence <m>] | Set Cue <n> [Sequence <m>] [FeatureGroup <g>] Fade|OutFade|Delay|OutDelay <s> | Set Cue <n> FeatureGroup <g> Path Linear|SCurve|EaseIn|EaseOut|Snap
```

A cue of a sequence (numbers may have decimals: Cue 1.5). `Cue 3` goes to it (Goto). Store Cue records the active programmer values; one equal to what tracks into the cue is kept as a blocked value. `At Release` stores a release. Without `Sequence <m>`, your selected sequence. Set gives the cue's timing: a dimmer going up and every other attribute use Fade/Delay, a dimmer going down OutFade/OutDelay; snap attributes (GDTF) jump after the delay. With `FeatureGroup <g>` the time is that group's own (`Cue` = back to the cue's), and its Path shapes its fades.

Examples:

```
Store Cue 1
Cue 3
Store Sequence 4 Cue 2
Set Cue 2 "Fade" 3
Set Cue 2 FeatureGroup "Position" "Path" SCurve
List Cue Sequence 4
```

Related: `sequence`, `go`, `goto`, `store`

Options:

- `/Merge` (Store): Add to what is there
- `/Overwrite (/o)` (Store): Replace what is there
- `/Remove` (Store): Take the selection out of what is there
- `/CreateSecondCue` (Store): Store as a new cue right after it
- `/Original` (Update): Where the value was stored (the cue it tracks from)
- `/Active` (Update): In this cue
- `/Shield` (Update): Protect the next cues: they keep their look

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Fade" | as its type declares | Program | show | fade in, seconds |
| "OutFade" | as its type declares | Program | show | fade out, seconds |
| "Delay" | as its type declares | Program | show | delay in, seconds |
| "OutDelay" | as its type declares | Program | show | delay out, seconds |
| "Paint" | #rrggbb, a palette colour, Theme "<slot>" or none | Program | show | its colour on screen: #rrggbb, a palette colour, Theme "<slot>" (the viewer's theme), or none = its tags', then the pool's |

## DataPool

aliases `datapools`, `pool`, `pools` · verbs List, Info, Select, Store, Delete, Edit, Copy, Update, Move · default verb Select (`DataPool <ids>` = `Select DataPool <ids>`) · rights Guest: List, Info · Playback: Select · Program: Store, Delete, Edit, Copy, Update, Move

```
DataPool <id | name> | <verb> DataPool <id | name> Group <n> …
```

A datapool: groups, presets, sequences, macros and other reusable show content. `Select DataPool <n>` makes it the one your pool objects resolve in (decisions §29); owner first, a line acts in another one without selecting it (`Delete DataPool 2 Group 3`) — what a pool window pinned to a DataPool sends.

```
Select DataPool 2

Store DataPool 2 Group 3
DataPool "Busk" Group 1
```

## DeskLock

verbs On, Off, Toggle · default verb Toggle (`DeskLock` = `Toggle DeskLock`) · rights Guest: On, Off, Toggle

```
DeskLock | On DeskLock [Station] | Off DeskLock | Toggle DeskLock
```

Lock this device (a desk lock): its screens show the lock surface, the station refuses its lines; playback, DMX, shells and other devices run on. F9 or Pause toggles it; a user with a password unlocks with it. `On DeskLock Station` locks every device of the station. Station-local, never replicated, not an Oops step (decisions §30 "12a3").

Examples:

```
DeskLock               -- toggle (F9 / Pause)
On DeskLock Station    -- lock every device of this station
```

Related: `desklock`, `normaltheme`, `sidebars`, `viewbar`, `fullscreen`


## Device

verbs Info · default verb Info (`Device <ids>` = `Info Device <ids>`) · rights Guest: Info

```
Device | Set Device "ScreenConfig" Follow|<n> | Reset Device
```

This device (every window of an app, or one browser tab; decisions §30 "12a3"). ScreenConfig: which of the user's screen configs it shows — Follow user (default) or a fixed number, e.g. a tablet on config 2. Station-local, never replicated, not an Oops step.

Examples:

```
Set Device "ScreenConfig" 2       -- this tablet always shows config 2
Set Device "ScreenConfig" Follow  -- back to the user's
```

Related: `desklock`, `normaltheme`, `screenconfig`

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "ScreenConfig" | 1–9999 or Follow | Guest | station | which of the user's screen configs this device shows (Follow = the user's) |


## DMX

verbs Info · default verb Info (`DMX <ids>` = `Info DMX <ids>`) · ids 2 parts · **planned — not built yet:** At · rights Guest: Info, At

```
DMX <universe>[.<address>] [/Input] | DMX <u>.<a> At <value> (planned) | Park DMX <u>.<a> | … At DMX [<u>[.<a>]]
```

A universe's DMX slots: DMX 2 is universe 2, DMX 2.001 one address (never the absolute number: DMX 513 is universe 513). Alone it shows what the engine outputs; /Input what the input lines bring in. After At it is where fixtures go: an address, the first free run in a universe, or a bare DMX for the first free run anywhere.

Examples:

```
DMX 1                            -- what universe 1 outputs
DMX 1.005                        -- one channel
DMX 1 /Input                     -- what the input lines bring in
Assign Fixture 201 At DMX 2.001  -- a fixture's address
Assign Fixture 201 Thru 206 At DMX 2   -- the first free run in universe 2
```

Related: `universe`, `park`, `assign`

Options:

- `/Input` (Info): What the input lines bring in, before it merges

| "Library" | Yes/No | Setup | station | whether LumaCore/library exists on it; Yes makes it (the first write does too); No is refused — a setting deletes nothing |

## EncoderBar

aliases `encoderbars` · verbs Store, Label, Delete, Move, List, Info, Edit · default verb Select (`EncoderBar <ids>` = `Select EncoderBar <ids>`) · **planned — not built yet:** Select · rights Guest: List, Info, Select · Playback: Store, Label, Delete, Move, Edit

```
Store [UserProfile] EncoderBar "name" | Label|Delete|Info EncoderBar <b> | List EncoderBar | Move [UserProfile] EncoderBar <b> FeatureGroup <g> At <n> | Attribute <a> At <n> | Edit EncoderBar
```

Your encoder bar layouts (decisions §30 "12f-a", an EncoderBarPool): a pool on your profile, each screen shows one. A layout is your groups as strip buttons with 4-slot pages; a new attribute lands at the bottom of its group's button on every layout. Attributes no patched fixture has stay in their slot, hidden on the bar.

Examples:

```
Store UserProfile EncoderBar "Busking"
Move UserProfile EncoderBar "Busking" FeatureGroup "Shutter" At 2
Move UserProfile EncoderBar "Busking" Attribute "Zoom" At 5
Info EncoderBar "Default"
Edit EncoderBar                                     -- Users & Profiles, Encoder bar tab
```

Related: `attribute`, `featuregroup`, `userprofile`


## Error

aliases `errors` · verbs List, Info · default verb Info (`Error <ids>` = `Info Error <ids>`) · rights Guest: List, Info

```
List Error [area] | Info Error <code>
```

Every error has a stable code (E-AREA-NNN) shown after its message. `Info Error <code>` explains it; `List Error` lists all codes, `List Error Patch` those of one area.

Examples:

```
info error E-PATCH-002   -- what an invalid DMX address means
list error               -- every code
list error cmd           -- command-line errors
```

## Fixture

aliases `fixtures`, `f` · verbs SelectFixtures, At, Store, Delete, Assign, Unassign, Edit, Move, Insert, Compact, Cut, Paste, List, Info, Dump, On, Off · default verb SelectFixtures (`Fixture <ids>` = `SelectFixtures Fixture <ids>`) · rights Guest: List, Info, Dump · Playback: SelectFixtures, At, On, Off · Program: Edit · Setup: Store, Delete, Assign, Unassign, Move, Insert, Compact, Cut, Paste · tree `Root.ShowData.Devices.Dmx.Patch.Fixtures`

## Group

aliases `groups`, `g` · verbs SelectFixtures, At, Store, Delete, Edit, Copy, Cut, Paste, Update, Move, Insert, Compact, List, Info, Dump, On, Off · default verb SelectFixtures (`Group <ids>` = `SelectFixtures Group <ids>`) · rights Guest: List, Info, Dump · Playback: SelectFixtures, At, On, Off · Program: Store, Delete, Edit, Copy, Cut, Paste, Update, Move, Insert, Compact · tree `Root.ShowData.DataPools.DataPool.Groups` · pool window

```
Group <n> [+ | - <selection>] [At <value>] | Group <n> Master At <v> [Fade <s>]
```

A stored selection in your datapool: members in order with grid spots (decisions §22). Calling it selects: a plain select adds to the selection until a value is set, then the next one replaces it (a common console convention); `+` always adds. A group can be a master (Set Group 3 "Mode" Positive / Negative / Scaling / Additive) whose level is `Master Group 3 At 50`. Store over an existing group needs /Merge, /Overwrite or /Remove.

Examples:

```
Group 1                      -- select group 1
Group 1 + Group 2 - Fixture 5
Group 3 At 50                -- select, then dimmer 50
Master Group 3 At 50 Fade 2  -- the group master
Store Group 4 /Merge
Set Group 4 "Mode" Scaling
```

Related: `store`, `select`, `plus`, `minus`, `grid`

Options:

- `/Merge` (Store, Copy, Paste): Add to what is there
- `/Overwrite (/o)` (Store, Copy, Paste): Replace what is there
- `/Remove` (Store): Take the selection out of what is there
- `/GridMerge <AppendX|Off>` (Store): Where merged members go in the grid
- `/By <key>` (Compact): What to sort, split, compact or show by (Number, Name, Family, MainFirst, Address, FixtureType)

## Identify

verbs On, Off · default verb On (`Identify` = `On Identify`) · rights Setup: On, Off

```
Identify [Fixture <ids> | DMX <u.a> [Thru <u.a>]] [/As Fixture <n>] | Off Identify [Fixture <ids> | DMX …]
```

Make fixtures or addresses show themselves on the rig: their GDTF defaults, the dimmer in a sine (15–100 %, 2 s), the colour round the hue circle (6 s; a wheel steps its slots). A probed address sends a 38–255 sine. Above programmers, playback, masters, Solo and input; Park wins. One per user; it ends with Off Identify, at logout and after 5 minutes. Station output only: never stored, never an Oops step.

Examples:

```
Identify Fixture 101 Thru 106     -- they flash on the rig
Identify                          -- your selection
Identify DMX 1.150                -- probe an address, patched or not
Identify DMX 1.043 Thru 1.056 /As Fixture 104   -- Find: the run in 104's shape
Off Identify                      -- end yours
```

Related: `dmx`, `fixture`, `park`, `highlight`

Options:

- `/As <fixture>` (On): Probe the run the way this fixture would show (Find)

## Master

aliases `masters` · verbs Info, At, List, On, Off, Toggle · default verb Info (`Master <ids>` = `Info Master <ids>`) · ids 2 parts · rights Guest: Info, List · Playback: At, On, Off, Toggle

```
Master 2.1|2.2|2.4|Highlight|Solo [At <0-100> | At + 10 …] | Master Highlight|Solo Mode Toggle|AlwaysOn|Disabled | On|Off|Toggle Master 2.1
```

Masters scale the output after the merge (the master groups, decisions §30 "12f"). Master 2.1 is the grand master: its level scales every intensity; switched Off it is a blackout (the level is kept). Master 2.2 / 2.4 cap everybody's Highlight / Solo; Master "Highlight" and Master "Solo" are yours (how strongly your Highlight and Solo act: Toggle, AlwaysOn or Disabled). Levels take relative input (At + 10, At * 2). Masters are never undone. Groups 1, 3, 4, 5 and 2.3 / 2.5 are planned.

Examples:

```
Master 2.1 At 80
Master 2.1 At - 10
Off Master 2.1   -- blackout
On Master 2.1
Master 2.4 At 50  -- Solo for everybody at half
Master "Highlight" At 50
Set Master "Solo" "Mode" AlwaysOn
Master Group 3 At 50 Fade 2
```

Related: `park`, `highlight`, `solo`

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Mode" | Toggle/AlwaysOn/Disabled | Playback | show | how your Highlight / Solo master acts: Toggle, AlwaysOn or Disabled (2.3 / 2.5) |

verbs Import (reach Drive), List, Info · default verb Info (`Mvr <ids>` = `Info Mvr <ids>`) · rights Guest: List, Info · Setup: Import

Options:

- `/Scope <target>` (Import): What the import works on: an MvrLayer, MvrGroup, MvrClass or Tag (absent: the whole patch)

- `/Z <mm>` (Import): The rig offset, Z (mm)
- `/Rotate <degrees>` (Import): The rig rotation about Z (degrees)
- `/Addresses <mode>` (Import): What the file may change in the addresses: None, Take, Offer
- `/Ids <mode>` (Import): What the file may change in the ids: None, Take, Offer
- `/Names <mode>` (Import): What the file may change in the names: None, Take, Offer
- `/Position <mode>` (Import): What the file may change in position and rotation: None, Take, Offer
- `/Revisions <mode>` (Import): What the file may change in the types' revisions: None, Take, Offer
- `/NewFixtures <mode>` (Import): The fixtures the file adds: None, Take, Offer
- `/Apply` (Import): Write the ticked rows of the review into the draft
- `/Cancel` (Import): Drop the review; the draft as it was
- `/Take <field>` (Import): Take one cell of a review row
- `/Offer <field>` (Import): Offer one cell of a review row again
- `/Gone <choice>` (Import): A new fixture's gone group: Recreate, Parent, None (`/Missing` is List Asset's)
- `/Group <name>` (Import): The one gone group a /Gone answer is for

## Preset

aliases `presets` · verbs List, Store, SelectFixtures, Delete, Update, Recast, Extract, Copy, Cut, Paste, Move, Insert, Compact · default verb SelectFixtures (`Preset <ids>` = `SelectFixtures Preset <ids>`) · rights Guest: List · Playback: SelectFixtures · Presets: Update · Program: Store, Delete, Recast, Extract, Copy, Cut, Paste, Move, Insert, Compact · tree `Root.ShowData.DataPools.DataPool.Presets` · pool window

```
Preset <n> | Store Preset [<n>] ["name"] [/Merge|/Overwrite|/Remove] | At Preset <n> | Call Preset <n> | Update Preset <n> [/Merge|/Add|/Overwrite] | Recast Preset <n> [Sequence <m>] | Extract Preset <n> [Sequence <m> [Cue <c>]]
```

The DataPool's one preset pool (decisions 0288). Store keeps every active value of your programmer (Selective: per fixture; Universal when every fixture holds the same value); At puts its values on the selected fixtures, Call is the same; a bare Preset selects its fixtures. Tag presets to sort them; the Presets window shows the ones that touch the feature group you are on. A cue stores a value from a preset as the link only and plays the preset as it is now (decisions 0293): Update puts your changes back into it, Recast brings its attributes into the cues that link it, Extract turns links into its values; deleting a used preset keeps the cues' values.

Examples:

```
Store Preset 3 "Deep red"   -- your active values as preset 3
Store Preset                 -- the next free number
At Preset 3                  -- its values on your selection
Preset 3                     -- select its fixtures
Assign Tag "Song 3" At Preset 3
Update Preset 3 /Merge        -- your changes back into it
Recast Preset 3              -- its new attributes into the cues
Extract Preset 3 Sequence 1  -- that sequence's links become values
```

Related: `store`, `at`, `tag`

Options:

- `/Merge` (Store, Update): Add to what is there
- `/Add` (Update): Also what isn't there yet (new attributes)
- `/Overwrite (/o)` (Store, Copy, Paste, Update): Replace what is there
- `/Remove` (Store): Take the selection out of what is there
- `/By <key>` (Compact): What to sort, split, compact or show by (Number, Name, Family, MainFirst, Address, FixtureType)

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Name" | text | Program | show | display name |
| "Note" | text | Program | show | operator note |
| "Locked" | On/Off | Program | show | protect from edits |
| "Hidden" | On/Off | Program | show | hide from operator views |
| "Paint" | #rrggbb, a palette colour, Theme "<slot>" or none | Program | show | its colour on screen: #rrggbb, a palette colour, Theme "<slot>" (the viewer's theme), or none = its tags', then the pool's |
| "Icon" | icon name | Program | show | a standard icon's name |

## Recovery

aliases `recoveries` · verbs List (reach Drive), Info (reach Drive), Delete (reach Drive) · default verb Info (`Recovery <ids>` = `Info Recovery <ids>`) · rights Guest: List, Info · Setup: Delete

```
List Recovery | Info Recovery "<copy>" | Set Recovery "<copy>" "Pinned" Yes|No | "Note" "text" | Delete Recovery "<copy>" | Delete Recovery /Cleanup
```

Recovery copies on this station (`library/shows/.autosave/`): the timed copy every Autosave minutes of a changed show, the copy before a load replaces unsaved work, and the copies kept on a stop signal or a lost merge. `LoadShow "x" /Recovery "<copy>"` opens one as unsaved changes. Cleanup follows the station's RecoveryKeepDays and RecoveryCap; pinned copies stay; deleted ones go to the trash for 30 days. After an unclean stop the station asks once when a copy is newer than the show file.

Examples:

```
List Recovery
LoadShow "demo" /Recovery "demo_timed_FOH_20261013-154700"
Set Recovery "demo_timed_FOH_20261013-154700" "Pinned" Yes
Delete Recovery /Cleanup     -- the cleanup rules now (asks)
```

Related: `version`, `show`, `loadshow`

Options:

- `/Cleanup`: Apply the station's cleanup rules now

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Pinned" | Yes/No | Program | station | never cleaned up |
| "Note" | text | Program | station | why it is kept (a note pins it) |

## Sacn

verbs Store, Delete, Copy, Cut, Paste, Move, Insert, Compact, List, Info, Assign, Unassign · default verb Info (`Sacn <ids>` = `Info Sacn <ids>`) · rights Guest: List, Info · Setup: Store, Delete, Copy, Cut, Paste, Move, Insert, Compact, Assign, Unassign · tree `Root.ShowData.Protocols.DMXProtocols.Lines`

```
Store Sacn [<n>] ["name"] /Network <name> [/Mode Output|Input] [/LocalUniverse <u> /Amount <n> /SacnUniverse <s>] | Assign Universe <u> Thru <v> At Sacn <n> [/Universe <s>] | Assign Sacn <n> At Universe <u> | Set Sacn <n> "Priority"|"SacnUniverse"|"Rate"|… <value>
```

An sACN (E1.31) line: one DMX Protocols row on its network — Mode Output sends its run of local universes (LocalUniverse and the Amount after it) as sACN universes from SacnUniverse on (multicast, or unicast to Target) at its own Rate; Mode Input brings those sACN universes into the local ones, at its InputPriority. Priority (0–200) is an output's. List Sacn shows each line's run and live state; Info Sacn the protocol.

Examples:

```
Store Sacn 1 "FOH" /Network "Rig" /LocalUniverse 1 /Amount 32 /SacnUniverse 101
Assign Universe 1 Thru 4 At Sacn 1 /Universe 101
Assign Sacn 2 At Universe 40 /Universe 9
Set Sacn 1 "Priority" 150
Set Sacn 1 "Rate" 44
Unassign Sacn 1
```

Related: `network`, `assign`, `universe`

Options:

- `/Network <network>` (Store): The network it is on
- `/Mode <mode>` (Store): Output (local universes go out) or Input (the protocol's come in)
- `/LocalUniverse <universe>` (Store): The first local universe the line carries
- `/Amount <count>` (Store): How many local universes from LocalUniverse
- `/SacnUniverse <universe>` (Store): The sACN universe LocalUniverse is on the wire; the rest follow on
- `/Universe <address>` (Assign): The protocol universe the run starts at (sACN n, Art-Net Net.SubNet.Universe)

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Name" | text | Setup | show | display name |
| "Note" | text | Setup | show | operator note |
| "Locked" | On/Off | Setup | show | protect from edits |
| "Hidden" | On/Off | Setup | show | hide from operator views |
| "Paint" | #rrggbb, a palette colour, Theme "<slot>" or none | Setup | show | its colour on screen: #rrggbb, a palette colour, Theme "<slot>" (the viewer's theme), or none = its tags', then the pool's |
| "Icon" | icon name | Setup | show | a standard icon's name |
| "Network" | Network name or number | Setup | show | the network the line uses (created if the show has none by that name) |
| "Mode" | Output/Input | Setup | show | Output (its local universes go out) or Input (the protocol's universes come in); Assign's order sets it too |
| "LocalUniverse" | 1–65535 | Setup | show | the first local universe the line carries (a universe by number: moving a universe never moves the line) |
| "Amount" | 0–4096 | Setup | show | how many local universes from LocalUniverse (0 = none) |
| "Target" | text | Setup | show | Output: unicast IPv4 address, none = multicast (sACN) / ArtPoll + broadcast (Art-Net). Input: accept only this source, none = any |
| "Rate" | 1–60 | Setup | show | Output: frames per second (1–60, default 30): the line samples the engine's newest 60 Hz frame; never above what an Art-Net node reports |
| "Send" | Full/Changes | Setup | show | Output: Full (every universe every time) or Changes (a change at once and 3 repeats, then a keep-alive every second) |
| "PacketGap" | 0–2000 | Setup | show | Output: µs between universes, for old nodes that drop bursts (0–2000; never more than half of one send period in all) |
| "Sync" | On/Off | Setup | show | Output: send ArtSync / an E1.31 sync packet after the line's universes (pixel and video nodes) |
| "InputPriority" | Super/Prog/Highest/High/LTP/Low/Lowest | Setup | show | Input: the band its DMX competes at in Prio universes (Super … Lowest) |
| "Enabled" | On/Off | Setup | show | the line runs |
| "SacnUniverse" | text | Setup | show | the Sacn universe LocalUniverse is on the wire; the rest follow on (1–63999) |
| "Priority" | 0–200 | Setup | show | Output lines only; E1.31 priority: a receiver takes the highest (0–200) (Sacn) |

## Tag

aliases `tags` · verbs SelectFixtures, Store, Label, Delete, Move, Assign, Unassign, List, Info, On, Off, Toggle, Go, Goto, Pause, At · default verb SelectFixtures (`Tag <ids>` = `SelectFixtures Tag <ids>`) · ids path (1.10 ≠ 1.1) · rights Guest: List, Info · Playback: SelectFixtures, On, Off, Toggle, Go, Goto, Pause, At · Program: Store, Label, Delete, Move, Assign, Unassign · tree `Root.ShowData.Tags`

```
Tag <path> [/R] | Store Tag [<path>] ["name"] | Label Tag <path> "name" | Delete Tag <path> [/WithChildren | /KeepChildren] | Move Tag <path> At Tag <path> | Root | <n> | Assign Tag <path> At <objects> | Unassign Tag <path> At <objects> | List Tag | Info Tag <path> [/R]
```

A tag in the tag tree: a tag has one parent and is numbered within it, so its number is its path (Tag 1.2.1 = the first child of the second child of tag 1). Any show object carries tags. A tag reaches the objects tagged with it; /R adds those of every tag under it. Alone it selects its fixtures.

Examples:

```
Store Tag "All"                     -- a top tag
Store Tag 1 Tag "Lx1"               -- a child of tag 1
Assign Tag 1.1 At Fixture 1 Thru 12   -- tag twelve fixtures
Tag 1.1                               -- select its fixtures
Tag 1 /R                              -- and those of every tag under it
Move Tag 1.2 At Tag 2                 -- put it under tag 2
Delete Tag 1.1 /KeepChildren          -- its child tags move up
```

Related: `group`, `assign`, `unassign`

Options:

- `/WithChildren` (Delete): Delete its child tags too
- `/KeepChildren` (Delete): Move its child tags up one level
- `/R` (SelectFixtures, Info, On, Off, Toggle, Go, Goto, Pause, At): Recursive: what is below too

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Action" | Default/Select | Program | show | what Run action does in the Tags window: the window's default, or Select (its fixtures) |
| "Name" | text | Program | show | display name, unique among its siblings |
| "Note" | text | Program | show | operator note |
| "Priority" | -1000–1000 | Program | show | an object without a Paint of its own takes the colour of its painted tag with the highest Priority (equal: the first in the tag tree) |
| "Paint" | #rrggbb, a palette colour, Theme "<slot>" or none | Program | show | its colour, and the colour of what it tags that has no Paint of its own: #rrggbb, a palette colour, Theme "<slot>", or none (its parent's) |

## User

aliases `users` · verbs Store, Delete, List, Info · default verb Info (`User <ids>` = `Info User <ids>`) · rights Guest: List, Info · Admin: Store, Delete · tree `Root.ShowData.Users`

```
User | Store User ["name" [/Rights r] [/Profile New|p] [/Password "pw"] [/Colour c]] | Set User "name" "Name"|"Password"|"Rights"|"Profile"|"Paint"|"RemoteLogin"|"ScreenConfig" <value> ("Password" Ask asks) | Delete User "name" [/WithProfile] [/NoConfirmation]
```

Users (ShowData.Users). A user owns their programmer and selection, has one rights level (Guest < Playback < Presets < Program < Setup < Admin, one ladder — rights come only from the user) and works in a profile (views, screens, keys, settings). A new user gets their own profile, a copy of the locked template Default, or shares one (never Default). A bare Store User asks; Delete User asks what goes (logs the user out everywhere, releases their claims; one Oops step). Store / Delete User and Set (but your own password and colour) need Admin; the user Admin is always Admin.

Examples:

```
User                                   -- list users
Store User                             -- asks: name, rights, profile, password, colour
Store User "LD" /Rights Program /Password "pw" /Colour Teal
Set User "LD" "Rights" Setup -- only an Admin grants levels
Store User "Phone" /Profile "LD"    -- share LD's views and screens
Set User "LD" "Name" "Anna"
Set User "LD" "Password" Ask -- asks (masked)
Delete User "LD" /WithProfile /NoConfirmation
```

Related: `login`, `logout`

Options:

- `/Rights <level>` (Store): The rights level
- `/Profile <profile>` (Store): The profile it uses (New, n or "name")
- `/Password <password>` (Store): Its password
- `/Colour <colour> (/Color)` (Store): Its colour
- `/WithProfile` (Delete): Delete its profile too
- `/None` (Set): No password

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Name" | text or Ask | Admin | show | the user's name (Ask opens the rename dialog) |
| "Password" | text or Ask | Guest | show | your own, or another user's as Admin; empty = none; Ask opens the dialog |
| "Rights" | Guest/Playback/Presets/Program/Setup/Admin | Admin | show | the user's level |
| "Paint" | text | Guest | show | the user's colour (a name or #rrggbb; your own, or another's as Admin) |
| "RemoteLogin" | On/Off | Admin | show | may log in from another machine |
| "Profile" | text or New | Admin | show | the profile the user works in (a name or number; New = a copy of Default) |
| "ScreenConfig" | 1–9999 | Admin | show | the screen config a new device of the user starts on |


## UserProfile

aliases `userprofiles`, `profile`, `profiles` · verbs Call, Store, List, Info, Dump, Import (reach Drive), Export (reach Drive), Delete, Label, Copy, Reset, Move, Edit, Assign · default verb Info (`UserProfile <ids>` = `Info UserProfile <ids>`) · rights Guest: Call, List, Info, Dump, Edit · Playback: Export, Reset, Move, Assign · Admin: Store, Import, Delete, Label, Copy · tree `Root.ShowData.UserProfiles`

```
List|Info UserProfile [<n>] | Store UserProfile ["name" [/CopyOf n]] | Copy UserProfile n At m|"name" | Label UserProfile n ["name"] | Delete UserProfile n [/NoConfirmation] | Set UserProfile [<n>|"name"] Theme.…|LockScreen.… <value> | "Export" UserProfile ["name"] | "Import" UserProfile ["file" [/As "Name" ] [/Overwrite]] | <verb> UserProfile [<n>|"name"] Image|Icon|WindowPreset … | Reset UserProfile [<n>|"name"] Window /Type <type>
```

How users work: views, screen configs, keys, settings — and the look, which travels with it (decisions §30 "12a2"): Theme (preset, adjusters, palette), LockScreen (picture, clock, text, auto-lock) and its own Icons and Images. No rights: those are the user's. UserProfile "Default" is the locked template (decisions §30 "12c2"): every new profile starts as a copy of it (never blank), it can't be changed, renamed or deleted and nobody works in it. Store / Copy / Label / Delete / Import a profile need Admin; a bare Store, Label or Import asks, Delete always asks and is refused while a user works in the profile. Export / Import moves a profile with its pictures to another show (/As = a copy with new GUIDs). A bare UserProfile is your own; its users and Admins may change it.

Examples:

```
Store UserProfile                    -- asks: name, from Default / copy of… / import file…
Store UserProfile "Stage" /CopyOf "Bob"
Copy UserProfile "Bob" At "Stage 2"
Delete UserProfile "Stage 2"        -- asks
Import UserProfile "Stage" /As "Stage 2"
Set UserProfile Theme "Base" Night
Set UserProfile Theme Paint "Accent" "#9a7a08"
Reset UserProfile "Bob" Theme
Import UserProfile Image "bg.jpg"
Set UserProfile LockScreen "Image" 1
Export UserProfile "Bob"
Import UserProfile "Bob" /Overwrite
UserProfile "Bob" WindowPreset 1  -- load Bob's preset 1 into this window
Reset UserProfile "Bob" Window /Type DMX -- every DMX window of the profile (asks)
```

Related: `user`, `image`, `icon`, `windowpreset`

Options:

- `/CopyOf <profile>` (Store): Start as a copy of this profile
- `/Overwrite (/o)` (Import): Replace what is there
- `/As <name>` (Import): Import it under this name
- `/Drive <id>` (Import, Export): The drive to read or write (List Drive); absent = the local library

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Name" | text | Admin | show | display name |
| "Note" | text | Guest | show | operator note |
| "Paint" | #rrggbb, a palette colour, Theme "<slot>" or none | Guest | show | its colour on screen: #rrggbb, a palette colour, Theme "<slot>" (the viewer's theme), or none = its tags', then the pool's |
| "PaintMode" | Palette/Free/Theme | Guest | show | the mode the paint picker opens on: the one you used last |

## Version

aliases `versions` · verbs List (reach Drive), Info (reach Drive), Delete (reach Drive) · default verb Info (`Version <ids>` = `Info Version <ids>`) · rights Guest: List, Info · Setup: Delete

```
List Version ["show"] | Info Version ["show"] <stamp> | Set Version "<stamp>" "Pinned" Yes|No | "Note" "text" | Delete Version ["show"] <stamp> [+ <stamp>]
```

A show's history and its versions: every save keeps the file it replaces in `library/shows/.versions/<show>/` (on this station), named by when it was saved. `List Version` is the show's history (one row per save: by, station, reason, changes, kept). A pinned version (a note pins it too) is never cleaned up. `LoadShow "x" /Version <stamp>` opens one as unsaved changes; `Import Show "x" /Version <stamp> …` takes parts of it.

Examples:

```
List Version                             -- the loaded show's history
List Version "Festival"                 -- another show's, without loading it
Set Version "20261013-113000" "Note" "before rehearsal"
LoadShow "demo" /Version 20261013-113000
```

Related: `show`, `recovery`, `saveshow`, `loadshow`

Options:

- `/Cleanup`: Apply the station's cleanup rules now

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Pinned" | Yes/No | Program | station | never cleaned up |
| "Note" | text | Program | station | why it is kept (a note pins it) |


## View

aliases `views` · verbs Call, Store, Delete, Label, Assign, List, Export (reach Drive), Import (reach Drive) · default verb Call (`View <ids>` = `Call View <ids>`) · rights Guest: Call, List · Playback: Store, Delete, Label, Assign, Export, Import · pool window

```
View [<n>] [/Screen <s>] | Export View <n> ["file"] | Import View "file" [<n>]
```

Recall a stored view onto a screen (screen). A view is a copy of a screen's windows, their placement and settings, stored on your user. Recall copies it back — editing windows afterwards does not change the stored view until you store it again. Without a number, lists your views.

Examples:

```
View                              -- list stored views and view buttons
View 3                            -- recall view 3 onto your first screen
View 3 /Screen 2                  -- recall onto screen 2
Store View 3 "Programming"      -- store the current screen as view 3
Delete View 3                     -- delete view 3
Assign View 3 At ViewButton 1.5   -- put view 3 on screen 1's button 5
Export View 3                     -- library/ui/views/<name>.json
Import View "Busk"                -- as your next free view
```

Related: `store`, `delete`, `assign`

Options:

- `/Screen <screen> (/s)` (Store, Call): The screen it is on
- `/Overwrite (/o)` (Store): Replace what is there
- `/Clear` (Store): Clear it

| Property | Value | Rights | Home | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Paint" | #rrggbb, a palette colour, Theme "<slot>" or none | Playback | show | its colour on screen: #rrggbb, a palette colour, Theme "<slot>" (the viewer's theme), or none = its tags', then the pool's |


## ViewBar

verbs On, Off, Toggle · default verb Toggle (`ViewBar` = `Toggle ViewBar`) · rights Guest: On, Off, Toggle

```
ViewBar | On ViewBar | Off ViewBar
```

Hide or show the view bar of this window (Meow+F10).

Examples:

```
ViewBar    -- toggle (Meow+F10)
```

Related: `desklock`, `normaltheme`, `sidebars`, `viewbar`, `fullscreen`


## ViewButton

aliases `viewbuttons`, `vb` · verbs Call, Store, Delete, Label, List · default verb Call (`ViewButton <ids>` = `Call ViewButton <ids>`) · ids 2 parts · rights Guest: Call, List · Playback: Store, Delete, Label

```
ViewButton [<screen>.]<n> [/Screen <s>]
```

A view bar button, per screen of your profile (decisions 0287): it holds any object — a view, a group, a sequence, a macro — and a tap runs that object's default verb (View 3, Select Sequence 4, the group's selection). A bare number is a button of the screen the line comes from. An empty button only says so; Store on it stores this screen as a new view there. With a pending command, tapping a view button completes it.

Examples:

```
ViewButton 1.4                      -- run what screen 1's button 4 holds
Assign Sequence 3 At ViewButton 1.6 -- put sequence 3 on it
Store ViewButton 1.4 "Busking"    -- store this screen into button 4
Label ViewButton 1.4 "Prog"       -- label the view it holds
Delete ViewButton 1.4               -- clear the button (the object stays)
```

Related: `view`, `store`, `assign`

Options:

- `/Screen <screen> (/s)` (Store): The screen it is on
- `/Overwrite (/o)` (Store): Replace what is there
- `/Clear` (Store): Clear it


## Watch

aliases `watches` · verbs Call, List · default verb Call (`Watch <ids>` = `Call Watch <ids>`) · rights Guest: Call, List

```
Watch <command | object> [/watch=<ms>] | List Watch
```

Watch any read-only command or object live with auto-refresh (a line that changes anything is refused). Default interval is 200ms. Objects (fixture, group, universe, selection, etc.) auto-expand to their list view. You can also use the `/watch` flag on any command directly. `List Watch` shows the running watches.

Examples:

```
watch selection        -- live selection view
watch fixture          -- live fixture list
watch clock            -- watch wall clock (200ms)
watch clock /watch=500 -- 500ms interval
list watch             -- running watches
```

Related: `unwatch`, `list`


## Window

aliases `windows` · verbs Select, Store, Label, Delete, Reset, List · default verb Select (`Window <ids>` = `Select Window <ids>`) · ids 2 parts · rights Guest: Select, List · Playback: Store, Label, Delete, Reset

```
Window [[screen.]n] | Store Window [n] "Type" [/Pane n] [/Overwrite] | Set Window [screen.]n <setting> <value>|+ n|- n|* n|Default|Toggle|Now | Set Window [screen.]n Maximized On|Off|Toggle | Reset Window [screen.]n
```

Windows on a screen (screen), addressed as [screen.]n. Window <n> focuses a window; bare Window lists this screen's windows. Store Window adds a window as a tab beside the focused one (or /Pane n); /Overwrite changes an existing window's type in place. Types are listed in Root.Resources.WindowTypes.

Examples:

```
Store Window "Groups"                -- add a Groups window beside the focused one
Store Window 5 "Terminal" /Overwrite -- change window 5 into a Terminal
Label Window 5 "Front"               -- tab title
Set Window 1.5 "Columns" 8           -- a window setting
Set Window 1.4 "Universe" + 1        -- relative; Toggle too
Reset Window 1.4 "Universe"          -- back to the type's default
Set Self "Maximized" On              -- hold this window full screen on the screen
Reset Window 1.4                     -- settings and bar back to the type's
Delete Window 2.*                    -- clear screen 2
```

Related: `view`, `store`, `set`

Options:

- `/Pane <pane> (/p)` (Store): The pane it goes in
- `/Screen <screen> (/s)` (Store): The screen it is on
- `/Overwrite (/o)` (Store): Replace what is there
- `/Clear` (Store): Clear it

## WindowPreset

aliases `windowpresets` · verbs Call, Store, Label, Delete, List, Info, Export (reach Drive), Import (reach Drive) · default verb Call (`WindowPreset <ids>` = `Call WindowPreset <ids>`) · rights Guest: Call, List, Info · Playback: Store, Label, Delete, Export, Import

```
Store WindowPreset [n] ["name"] [/Overwrite] | WindowPreset [n] | Label|Delete|Info|Export WindowPreset n | Import WindowPreset "file" | List WindowPreset [/Type t] | UserProfile [<n>|"name"] WindowPreset …
```

A window's look and settings kept on your profile, per window type: everything of a window — its settings, window bar, label, colour and scroll. Store saves Self's window (the window the line belongs to; /Window [screen.]n names one), WindowPreset n copies one into it (no live link: the window only remembers where it came from). A bare Store WindowPreset / WindowPreset asks. Presets travel with Export UserProfile; Export / Import WindowPreset use JSON in library/ui/windowpresets/.

Examples:

```
Store WindowPreset "Big DMX"        -- this window as a new preset
WindowPreset 2                      -- load preset 2 into this window
Store WindowPreset 2 /Overwrite      -- replace preset 2
Label WindowPreset 2 "Patch check"
List WindowPreset /Type DMX
UserProfile "Bob" WindowPreset 1    -- load Bob's preset 1
Export WindowPreset 2
```

Related: `self`, `window`, `userprofile`

Options:

- `/Window <window> (/w)`: The window it comes from or goes to
- `/Type <type> (/t)`: The window type
- `/Overwrite (/o)` (Store): Replace what is there
